* **“iPhone 16 is a flop” is premature:** As of August 6, 2024, the iPhone 16 has not been announced or released. Apple’s Q3 FY24 10-Q (ended June 29, 2024) reflects the June announcement of iOS 18 and Apple Intelligence [E8], ahead of Apple’s typical fall hardware cycle, and notes that channel inventory of older models often declines before new launches [E11].
* **“Lost the AI race” misreads the strategy:** Rather than competing in external cloud-capex races, Apple is embedding Apple Intelligence across iOS 18, macOS Sequoia, and iPadOS 18 [E8, E14] to monetize an active installed base that reached an all-time high across all geographic segments in Q3 FY24 [E14], backed by $8,006 million [E8] in quarterly R&D (+7.58% [C16] YoY).

Even if a large institutional trim occurred, reducing a concentrated, appreciated stake at 31.49x [C9] trailing P/E reflects portfolio sizing or valuation discipline rather than operational failure.
* **Fundamentals contradict the Nokia comparison:** Nokia’s margins and cash flows imploded as a hardware-only vendor. In Q3 FY24, Apple posted June-quarter record revenue of $85.78 billion [E1] (+4.87% [E1] YoY), diluted EPS of $1.40 [E1] (beating the $1.34 [E25] estimate by +4.48% [E25]), and a 46.26% [E1] gross margin. TTM free cash flow stands at $104.34 billion [C5].

### Conclusion
Apple ($AAPL) is not becoming the next Nokia: its business shows expanding gross margins (46.26% [E1] in Q3 FY24), a high-margin recurring Services engine (74.00% [C14] gross margin), and $104.34 billion [C5] in trailing twelve-month free cash flow. *This is research, not investment advice.*
